IR.rationale: A rising intermediate yield relative to the policy rate signals a repricing of the expected rate path. That hits the duration component of HY and EM sovereign bonds and tends to persist for a few weeks.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads raise the forward risk premium. Spread shocks partly mean-revert, which lifts subsequent excess returns on risky debt.

V.rationale: High equity implied volatility marks elevated risk-bearing prices. Credit and EM debt earn higher subsequent returns as compensation.

AP.rationale: Strong equity weeks tend to be priced into credit quickly. Bonds then partly give back gains as equity-driven risk appetite fades.

ST.rationale: Strong momentum returns reflect crowded trend-following risk-on positioning. Its later unwinding weighs on lower-quality credit.

FX.rationale: A strengthening dollar tightens global dollar funding and EM balance sheets. That depresses USD-denominated EM and high-yield debt returns.

COM.rationale: Rising commodity prices support energy and materials issuers in HY and commodity-exporting EM sovereigns.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions restrict credit supply and refinancing. That predicts weaker returns for risky debt.

ENDG.rationale: Credit indices show short-horizon return autocorrelation from stale pricing and slow information diffusion, with partial reversal after extremes.

IR.rationale: Upward shifts in near-term policy expectations raise rate uncertainty. That uncertainty spills into risky bond price variability.

B.rationale: Joint selloffs in HY and EM debt indicate a broad credit shock. Through leverage and liquidity effects, such shocks raise future variance beyond its own history.

V.rationale: Simultaneously elevated equity and gold implied volatility signals broad cross-asset uncertainty. Implied volatility forecasts realised variance beyond its own lags.

AP.rationale: Falling developed and EM equities together indicate a global risk-off shock. Through the leverage effect this raises subsequent credit volatility.

ST.rationale: Strong profitability-factor returns reflect flight to quality within equities. That accompanies rising risk aversion and turbulence.

FX.rationale: Dollar appreciation tightens global financing conditions and stresses EM borrowers, raising volatility in USD-denominated risky debt.

COM.rationale: Commodity price declines stress energy-heavy HY issuers and commodity-exporting sovereigns, raising future price variability.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions reduce dealer balance-sheet capacity and liquidity. That amplifies subsequent price swings.

ENDG.rationale: Variance is persistent, but the residual after own-lag prediction tends to mean-revert when recent variance is extreme.

IR.rationale: Bear steepening raises long yields and term premia. That hits the duration of EM sovereign and HY bonds and can trigger outflow-driven drawdowns.

B.rationale: Weak EM sovereign debt returns signal fund outflows and deteriorating sentiment. These tend to cluster and precede further tail losses.

V.rationale: Broad cross-asset implied volatility widens the return distribution. That raises the probability of tail losses.

AP.rationale: EM equity weakness leads EM credit and signals global growth and risk-appetite deterioration.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors carry no clear mechanism for credit tail losses.

FX.rationale: Dollar surges tighten EM and leveraged-borrower financing, a classic trigger of EM debt drawdowns.

COM.rationale: Precious-metal rallies reflect hedging demand and rising perceived tail risk.

MC.rationale: Joint tight conditions and elevated stress mark a fragile regime in which forced selling and illiquidity produce large losses.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent returns signal a stressed regime in which losses tend to cluster.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields relative to the policy rate indicate easing expectations. These support strong duration and credit rallies.

B.rationale: After spread widening, elevated risk premia make sharp rebounds more likely as spreads mean-revert.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the distribution and coincides with high risk premia. Both raise the chance of large relief rallies.

AP.rationale: Strong EM equity returns signal improving global risk appetite. EM sovereign and HY credit tend to follow.

ST.rationale: Momentum losses typically occur in sharp junk-led rebounds after stress. These coincide with large credit rallies.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar eases global dollar funding and EM financing conditions, fostering strong EM debt returns.

COM.rationale: Oil rebounds lift energy-heavy HY issuers and oil-exporting sovereigns sharply.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress means depressed prices and high risk premia. When stress abates, recoveries are large.

ENDG.rationale: Large gains in credit often follow poor returns, as oversold markets rebound.
